eligibility: Foreign individual: passport, transaction-amount source evidence and tax voucher. No universal $50k hard cap.
pros_cons: Can remit documented income; paperwork and bank review.
steps: Collect contract, payslips and tax records; confirm classification and documents with bank; buy USD; wire to own account; retain receipts.

eligibility: Foreign permanent residence ID holders qualify for purchase quota; confirm eligibility and permitted purpose.
pros_cons: Simple inside quota; not a blanket route for every passport holder.
steps: Confirm PRC permanent resident ID and unused quota with bank; provide ID and truthful purpose; convert and remit with bank approval.

eligibility: Original exchange receipt valid 24 months; ID-only thresholds apply to genuinely unused exchanged RMB.
pros_cons: Useful for identifiable unused exchange; receipt and time restriction.
steps: Locate original exchange slip; establish unused balance and date; present passport and slip; convert and arrange lawful wire.

eligibility: Bank checks transfer completion, tax documents and net proceeds; 2025 capital-account guide §8.
pros_cons: Eligible net sale proceeds may be remitted; sale, tax and documentary costs vary.
steps: Complete genuine sale and title transfer; obtain contract and tax proof; seek bank review of net share; convert and remit.

eligibility: Foreign heir applies through appropriate SAFE branch; specific evidence and tax documentation required.
pros_cons: Route for qualifying inheritance; approval and proof required.
steps: Gather death, inheritance, ownership and tax documentation; apply to competent SAFE branch; present approval to bank; remit to own overseas account.

eligibility: Narrow eligibility for pre-emigration property; 2014 reform removed mandatory staging.
pros_cons: May remit approved assets in one or several payments; not available to everyone.
steps: Document emigration, eligible pre-emigration assets and tax; apply to competent SAFE branch; bank remits approved amount to own overseas account.

eligibility: Applies only if already held in foreign currency, not CNY; check account classification.
pros_cons: Avoids another CNY conversion; wire and receiving costs still apply.
steps: Confirm foreign-currency balance and source; provide identification and any required evidence; instruct bank to wire; retain confirmation.

eligibility: Specific route, bank acceptance, RMB receiving account and offshore conversion quote must be confirmed.
pros_cons: Potential offshore pricing; two legs, fees and authorization uncertain.
steps: Ask both banks in writing about applicable category and permitted RMB cross-border transfer; compare firm all-in quotes; proceed only if approved.

eligibility: Domestic cards combined: RMB 100,000 equivalent per person per calendar year; RMB 10,000 per card per day.
pros_cons: Cash access; caps, ATM and FX fees; not a bulk wire replacement.
steps: Verify card overseas access and fees; withdraw within applicable limits; keep records; do not borrow cards to evade limits.

eligibility: China departure rules depend on amount and declaration history; U.S. reporting applies above $10,000.
pros_cons: Cash is portable but loss risk, permits and reporting make it unsuitable for bulk transfers.
steps: Lawfully acquire foreign cash; check China exit permit and prior declaration; report over $10,000 on U.S. entry using FinCEN 105; retain proof.

eligibility: Only genuine distributable company profits; applicable tax and corporate approvals vary.
pros_cons: Not a way to relabel a personal deposit; corporate tax and paperwork.
steps: Confirm company ownership and distributable profits; obtain resolutions, audit and tax documents; ask bank for eligible dividend remittance process.

eligibility: Provider eligibility and quote depend on service; bank FX rules still apply.
pros_cons: May be convenient; no verified personalized rate or eligibility.
steps: Ask licensed provider and partner bank about passport eligibility, source documents, limits and written total quote; use only approved service.

eligibility: Splitting to evade convenience or authenticity controls is prohibited.
pros_cons: No lawful advantage; watchlist and penalties possible.
steps: Do not use; obtain legitimate documentation and request bank guidance.

eligibility: SAFE warns private online or informal exchange is illegal.
pros_cons: Potential confiscation, penalties and fraud risk.
steps: Do not use; use licensed institutions and truthful documents.

eligibility: PBOC 2026 notice prohibits mainland fiat-to-virtual-currency exchange business.
steps: Do not use as a workaround; consult licensed bank about lawful route.
